questions.text: How soon would you like this business to have a realistic chance of making money?

options.text: As soon as reasonably possible. I would rather start with something I can sell without months of development.
I can spend a few weeks getting something ready if it gives me a better fit.
I am comfortable spending a few months building or developing something before I sell it.
I am willing to take a longer path if it means creating something I really want to own.
I am not sure.

questions.text: How much money are you comfortable putting into a business before you know whether customers will actually buy?

options.text: As close to $0 as possible.
A few hundred dollars.
Around $1,000 to a few thousand dollars if the idea makes sense.
I am comfortable making a larger investment for the right opportunity.
I am not sure yet.

questions.text: Realistically, how much time can you give this business most weeks?

options.text: Less than 5 hours.
About 5 to 10 hours.
About 10 to 20 hours.
More than 20 hours.
It varies so much that I need something flexible.

questions.text: How involved would you like to be with customers personally?

options.text: Very little. I would rather the product do most of the work.
Some interaction is fine, but I do not want customers depending heavily on me.
I like working directly with people and helping them get a result.
Personal interaction is one of the parts I would enjoy most.
I am not sure.

questions.text: Imagine you suddenly make 100 sales instead of 10. What would you most want to happen to your workload?

options.text: I want the extra sales to create very little extra work.
Some extra work is fine, but I do not want my workload to grow anywhere near ten times.
I am comfortable doing substantially more work if I am making substantially more money.
I would rather serve fewer customers personally and potentially charge more for that involvement.
I have not thought about this.
I would rather start by selling or recommending something that already exists.
I like the idea of taking an existing kind of product and creating my own version of it.
I want to create something from my own knowledge, skills, or creativity.
I would love to create something genuinely new that does not already exist.
I am not sure.

questions.text: If both had equal income potential, which sounds more appealing to work with?

options.text: Digital products or experiences. I like the idea of little or no physical inventory.
Physical products. I like the idea of selling something tangible.
I could happily do either.
I like businesses that combine physical and digital elements.
I am not sure.

questions.text: How do you feel about buying, storing, packing, making, or otherwise handling physical products?

options.text: I want as little of that as possible.
I could handle a small amount if the business made sense.
I am comfortable with inventory and physical fulfillment.
Making or handling the product myself actually sounds enjoyable.
I am not sure.

questions.text: You find a product people genuinely want. Which situation sounds best?

options.text: I want to own and control the product, even if that means I am responsible for more of the business.
I would rather another company handle the product and much of the infrastructure while I focus on connecting customers with it.
I want something in between: a product that is mine without having to personally manufacture everything.
I care more about whether the opportunity works for me than who technically owns the product.
I am not sure.

questions.text: How important is it that the same customer can create income for you more than once?

options.text: Very important. I would strongly prefer a model where customers can continue generating revenue.
I would like repeat income, but it is not required.
I am comfortable continually finding new buyers for one-off purchases.
I care more about the total economics than whether the money comes from new or returning customers.
I am not sure.

questions.text: If a customer pays you again, which reason sounds most appealing?

options.text: They used up a product and need more.
They keep paying because they continue receiving access, content, tools, community, or support.
They continue hiring me because I provide an ongoing service.
They may buy again, but I do not need repeat purchases built into the model.
I am not sure.
Start with skills, knowledge, equipment, or experience I already have.
Mostly use what I already know, but learn a few new things along the way.
I am excited to learn a new business model or develop a new capability.
I am willing to spend substantial time learning or developing something if I believe in it.
I am not sure what I already know that someone would pay for.

questions.text: Which role sounds most like something you would enjoy?

options.text: Creating useful things people can buy.
Finding good products or resources and connecting the right people with them.
Personally helping someone solve a problem or get a result.
Building the systems, brand, and operation behind a product.
More than one of these sounds appealing.

questions.text: What are you hoping this business can eventually do for you?

options.text: Bring in some useful extra money.
Become a meaningful second income.
Potentially replace a job or primary income.
Grow into something larger than what I can personally deliver by myself.
I do not know yet. I mostly want to start.

questions.text: If you could only optimize for ONE of these right now, which would you choose?

options.text: Start with the least money and financial risk I reasonably can.
Get to something sellable as quickly as I reasonably can.
Build something I own and control.
Build something that has the potential to become less dependent on my personal time.
I honestly do not know yet.

priorityTieBreaker.text: You have said that several things matter to you. If they conflict, which one matters most right now?
priorityTieBreaker.help: This final question is built from your own answers. It is a tie-breaker, not a new category.
